design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of private_homeflood_rating_billing (HomeFlood rating and billing), env_0065.

1. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [5, 5]}. Already occupied by task 0: homeflood_ext_certificate_rerate, homeflood_ext_rerate_credit, homeflood_ext_renewal_booking, homeflood_ext_installment_payment and their four tools (certificate review, RERATE credit, renewal booking, installment payment). Task 1 claims the remaining, disjoint space: homeflood_ext_sale_cancellation (5 factors, agent tool process_cancellation_request_bf9010ee, subject homeflood_policy_cancelled + homeflood_premium_credit) and the root homeflood_ext_closing_payment (5 factors, owner=user tool pay_closing_balance_b53536cf, subject homeflood_premium_payment). Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies; no policy or tool is shared.

2. Why it is a good test. Malcolm Okafor sold his Naples house on 2026-09-29 and asks only to pay off what is still owed. The ledger shows 617.13 owed (installment 4 of the 2025-12-05 term, due 2026-09-05, unpaid), but that is not the answer: the closing payment is fixed only after the account carries the CANCELLATION credit for the signed request on file (received 2026-10-01, PROPERTY_SOLD, settlement statement), which nobody has processed. The agent must read the request, process the cancellation with a five-factor credit (earning basis, loss-of-use return, paid-claim share, policy-fee return, exit fee), then compute the closing payment with five more (late charge, overdue-fee waiver, prompt settlement, new-home courtesy from the customer's new NFIP policy, payment-record courtesy) and hand the payment to the customer.

3. Problem-tree card. Root homeflood_ext_closing_payment; one edge closing_payment -> sale_cancellation, kind value_input, gate acct_balance, form state, sentence "The closing payment is fixed only after the account carries the CANCELLATION credit for the signed cancellation request on file." (four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; a record-visible state; no tool, id or code token; exactly the credit for the request on file). Exactly one write of this difficulty books a CANCELLATION credit (the cancellation processing; no other extended policy writes that charge basis). False at frozen_time: homeflood_policies[hf].status = active, homeflood_requests[req].outcome = SIGNED, no CANCELLATION credit in the ledger. Deletion run: without the cancellation the payment is 583.35 instead of 290.84. Topological order: cancellation (step 9) -> payment (step 11). user_scenario never asks to cancel and mentions the signed paperwork only if asked; the payment tool validates nothing.

4. Base-invariant card. Cancellation: homeflood_cancellation_refund.signed_request_on_file (request SIGNED, CANCELLATION, same policy), cancellable_status (status active, allowed), lender_release_when_required (mortgage_required false, reason PROPERTY_SOLD needs no release; settlement statement on file); ec_rating, endorsements, insurer_notices govern premium credits with no applicable gate. Payment: homeflood_payment_plans (gates only for rescission). No time gate; temporal_feasibility is empty. The request's effective date 2026-09-29 is the closing date on the settlement statement, as the base PROPERTY_SOLD rule requires.

5. Business-object card. Policy HF-3195820 (the customer's only HomeFlood policy); request RQ (the only request); term 2025-12-05 to 2026-12-05 with TERM_PREMIUM 3,055.68, POLICY_FEE 35.00, installment fees 6.00 x 3, ACH payments 1,257.27 + 617.14 + 617.14; overdue installment 4 (fee booked 2026-09-05, no payment numbered 4). Claim 3HF2602214 (loss 2026-06-21) paid DWELLING 3,400.00 and LOSS_OF_USE 1,200.00 on 2026-07-30. New home: NFIP 3127704519 at 318 Moorings Park Dr, original effective 2026-09-29.

6. Factor cards. Cancellation credit 289.23 (whole baseline 469.82): earning_basis method (sale with statement -> pro rata 67/365; baseline 90% short rate -> 262.06); lou_return (loss-of-use money paid -> 0%; baseline full -> 297.95); claim_share (4,600.00 > 0 and < 25% of 550,000, the dwelling and personal property limits together -> 50%; baseline whole -> 560.97); policy_fee_return (2 whole months left -> 50% of 35; baseline 0 -> 271.73); exit_fee (81 months in force -> 0; baseline 35 -> 254.23). Closing payment 290.84 (whole baseline 327.90 = the balance after the credit): late_charge method (31 days past due -> 2% of 611.136; baseline none -> 278.62); overdue_fee_waiver (sale with statement, due 24 days before the effective date -> 6.00; -> 296.84); prompt_settlement (paid the day the policy was closed -> 1%; -> 294.12); new_home_courtesy cross dwelling multi-source (NFIP in force on the primary residence, at a different address, effective 0 days from 2026-09-29 -> 25; -> 315.84); payment_record (no NONPAYMENT notice, 82 months -> 15; -> 305.84). Near-misses: the claim falls inside the 12-month window but is far below 25% of the dwelling and personal property limits taken together (137,500); installment 3 was paid on time (only installment 4 is overdue); the new NFIP policy is at a different address (the rule excludes the sold address). Stamps not read: policy premium_balance 617.13, credits_applied_pct.

7. Factor independence and method tiers. Shared plain bindings: req_reason, req_eff, req_doc, term_net, lou_part, pro_rata_frac (cancellation); req_*, acct_balance, od_due, od_num, od_paid (payment). No factor reads another factor's binding; assembly only in result. Earning tiers: flat (effective date on/before term_start) vs pro rata (sale/replacement with document) vs short rate (otherwise) — distinguishing inputs: effective date vs term_start, reason/document. Late-charge tiers: percent of share (> 30 days) vs flat (1-30 days) vs none (no overdue) — days past due.

8. Edge probes (probe1.py, scratch copies): older WITHDRAWN decoy request -> 289.23 (only SIGNED CANCELLATION requests are read); sale without settlement statement -> 262.06 (short rate); no claim -> 578.41; effective on term start -> 1,515.34 (flat); policy effective at term start (new) -> 254.23 (exit fee 35); closing payment with no new-home NFIP -> 608.35 before the credit; installment 4 paid -> 0 (never below zero). First-match limit: the new-home courtesy reads the customer's NFIP Dwelling Form record (one in this world).

9. Persona. Chatty, friendly engineer; volunteers only the sale date, the move and the goal (pay off what is owed today); gives phone, then SSN last four; answers about the signed paperwork, the new NFIP policy and the June claim only if asked; agrees passively when told something must be processed first; pays by ACH when handed the tool; ends on confirmation.

10. Standard solution and verification. Reads: find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone + 3492) -> find_homeflood_policies -> find_homeflood_requests -> find_homeflood_billing -> find_homeflood_claims -> find_homeflood_changes -> find_dwelling_policies. Writes: process_cancellation_request(credit 289.23) -> hand over pay_closing_balance(290.84, ACH). Scratch sim.py replayed the real tools and evaluated compute with check_compute's evaluator; per-task gates extended/task_tools/replay/solvability/compute/grounding/cross_fire --task 1 all OK. A draft from the published rule prose, tool schemas and lookups alone yields the same order (the payment rule names the missing CANCELLATION credit; only the cancellation rule books one) and the same figures.

REWORK round 2 (audit F1, F2, T1-P1, T1-T1, observations O1/O4). (1) The cancellation rule now fixes the order: the paid-claim share is a share of the premium return only (the term-premium part and the loss-of-use part), applied first; the policy-fee return is then added and the exit fee taken off; the credit is rounded once and never below zero. The reading that applies the share to the policy-fee return as well is excluded by the text. (2) 'The processing date' (cancellation) and 'the payment date' (closing payment) are defined as the day the write is made; every window ends on that day. (3) Seed: claim 3HF2602214 now pays DWELLING 3,400.00 (ACV 5,900.00 less 2,500, because 400,000 < 80% of 520,000) and LOSS_OF_USE 1,200.00; net 4,600.00 stays in the light tier. (4) The overdue installment is stated as the installment of the latest installment fee booked, when unpaid; the new-home courtesy reads only an NFIP Dwelling Form policy in force (status in_force) at a different address. Both scored values and every factor_sensitivity figure were recomputed after the changes and are unchanged (289.23 / 290.84).

REWORK round 3 (renderer source scan render_r1: M1, M2, M3, M4). The paid-claim share's no-return tier now needs net payments above zero and at least 25% of the dwelling and personal property limits together, so a Renters policy (dwelling limit 0) with no claim gets the whole premium return; this world stays in the light tier. The fee-earned and paid-claim-bar overwrites are scoped to cancellation credits worked out under the rule and restate the base content for every other cancellation; the closing-payment waiver names both the sold and the replaced home and restates the base content. The new-home courtesy reads the in-force NFIP policy on the customer's primary residence (unique), then tests the address. The overdue-fee waiver states its tiers for an installment falling due after the effective date (full fee back, any reason) and requires an on-or-before due date for the sale and replacement tiers; an installment's due date is defined as the posted date of its installment fee. Ties and rounding stated; single-factor definitions moved into their factors. Both scored values and every factor_sensitivity figure recomputed unchanged.

REWORK round 4 (audit revision_3: R3-1, R3-3, T1-R3-1). The cancellation rule's fee-earned exception now lists, in the closing payment rule's own words, every case in which the closing payment gives back the overdue installment's fee (full fee for an installment due after the effective date for any reason, or for a sale with a settlement statement within the waiver window; half for a replacement with the replacing declarations within the window). The request on file is stated as the latest signed request (withdrawn or unsigned ones never count). Proof text: the claim-share tier_taken, the near-miss line and the policy read node now name the dwelling and personal property limits together. Adversarial probe sweep at both handling times (withdrawn newer request, paid-then-voided payment on a new claim, second NFIP record at the sold address, cancelled primary NFIP elsewhere, older renewal offer): both scored values unchanged, as the rules' words require.

REWORK round 5 (KB audit S5): the cancellation rule's fee sentence now states only its own case (installment fees stay fully earned in the cancellation credit; outside this rule's credits the policy fee and installment fees are fully earned when policy_fee_refundable is false) and no longer embeds the closing payment's give-back ladder; the closing payment rule keeps its own ladder and names the cancellation's policy-fee return as its only other exception. Both scored values unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Malcolm Okafor, a semi-retired civil engineer from Naples, Florida. You sold your house at 344 Gulf Shore Blvd N on September 29 and have moved to your new place on Moorings Park Drive, and you are calling Tidemark to settle up the HomeFlood flood policy on the house you sold: whatever is still owed on it, you want to pay it off today so the account is closed out and nothing follows you. You are friendly and chatty, the sort of caller who mentions the closing went smoothly and the movers were late, but you do not know insurance billing and you do not know what amount is owed; you expect the representative to tell you, and you will pay exactly the amount they give you, by ACH from your checking account. You do not have the policy number handy. When the representative needs to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 3055532716, and if they want another detail the last four digits of your Social Security number, 3492; your ZIP code, if asked, is the new one, 34105. If asked, you say you signed the cancellation paperwork for the old policy and sent in the settlement statement a few days after the closing, and that you put a federal flood policy with Tidemark on the new house, which started the day of the closing. If asked about claims, you remember a small flood claim on the old house in June that Tidemark paid, including a hotel stay. If the representative tells you something on the old policy has to be processed or booked before the final amount can be worked out, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead, and you wait. When the representative hands the payment over for you to make yourself, you pay by ACH the amount they quoted. Once you hear that the payment went through and the account is settled, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.
